order: Score a blind validation pass against the pre-registered follow-on corpus and record every disagreement in a ledger. The independent pass must be completed and saved before the sealed corpus file is ever opened; scoring after unsealing would invalidate the pass and must never be accepted as the recorded result. Compare the pass item by item against the reference scoring and report the match rate against the pre-registered threshold. For each disagreement, name the two candidate classes and state whether it reflects a genuine ambiguity in the boundary rule or a flaw found in the corpus item itself — flag only the one at the ambiguity cap as genuine, and record it as exactly one ambiguity, not more. If the match rate falls short of the threshold, trigger the pre-registered next step — a further boundary redraw — before the taxonomy is treated as validated for encoding downstream.
claims: The independent pass scored 17 of 20 (85 percent) against the pre-registered corpus, missing the threshold. Three disagreements were logged in the ledger — one on an evidence-class pair, exactly one flagged as a genuine ambiguity at the ambiguity cap, and one on a diagnosis-class pair — with no flaw found in any corpus item itself. Per the pre-registered rule, a second boundary redraw was triggered before the taxonomy proceeds to downstream encoding; the change touched two files with 62 insertions and 32 deletions.
